sn6.10:1.1: This discourse has an exact parallel at [an10.89]() and an extended parallel at [snp3.10](). One difficult problem of these texts is the meaning of the numbers counting the duration of hell. The extended version has an extra method of calculating this which is essential to decode them, so I discuss them there and summarize here.
sn6.10:6.2: Ten hells are listed here, the names of which do not correspond with the 21 or 28 listed in Purāṇas, nor with the seven Jain hells, nor with the hells of [mn130](). The commentary offers three explanations for the obscure names of these hells: they are numbers reflecting the duration spent in Avīci; or they are the cries uttered by those suffering there; or they are simply the cold hells.
sn6.10:6.3: The Sanskrit _nyarbuda_ is said rather to be ten times the _arbuda_. Normally number sequences in Indian texts multiply by ten, so it seems the “twenty” here is meant to reinforce the greatness of the magnitude.
sn6.10:6.9: The _sogandhika_ is variously identified as blue or white.
sn6.10:6.11: Assuming the smaller _arbuda_ of ten million, the Pink Lotus lasts for 5.12×10¹⁸ years.
